title: Checkmate
summary: Check with no escape ends the game. Learn to recognise it.

steps.md: **Checkmate** = the king is in check **and** none of the three escapes works (no safe square, no capture of the checker, no block). The game ends immediately: the side that gives mate wins.
Checkmate. The queen on d7 checks; the black king cannot take it because the white king guards it, and every flight square is covered.

steps.question: Is this checkmate?
choices: No, the king can capture the queen
No, it is not even check
steps.explain: The queen on d7 is undefended (the white king on d5 is too far away). Kxd7 escapes.

steps.question: Black to move. Check, checkmate, or neither?
steps.explain: The rook checks on the back rank, and the black pawns on f7, g7, h7 take away every escape square. This is the back-rank mate.
The queen checks along the 8th rank; your king on d6 covers c7, d7 and e7. Qa8# works too.
Re8#: the black king is boxed in by its own pawns. You will meet this back-rank pattern again and again.

steps.question: Black to move. What is the situation?
choices: Check, but not mate: the king can step off the 8th rank
steps.explain: The rook checks along the 8th rank, but the king can step to d7, e7 or f7 (all unguarded). Before you announce mate, test all three escapes.

steps.question: Retrieval check: checkmate means...
choices: Check, and no legal move escapes it
The king has no moves but is not in check
steps.explain: Check + no escape. Without the check, it would be stalemate (next lesson).

steps.question: Retrieval check: what happens after checkmate?
choices: The game ends; the mating side wins
The king is captured next move
Play continues until the king is taken
steps.explain: Mate ends the game at once.
